To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. # Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Basis:** Seller's update draft and Disclosure Letter, reviewed against our internal Buyer playbook

## Overview

The Seller's package moves sharply against us on almost every point. It is not "fair and balanced." Three features stand out:

1. **It adopts our fallback positions as its opening.** The 20% cap and 18-month claims period are our conditional fallbacks. Amelia Frost has not authorised either, so we cannot accept them.
2. **It folds the protected regimes into the general one.** Title, capacity, fraud, Tax and IP would all sit under the general limitations through blanket "all Claims" drafting.
3. **It leaves the three main completion risks open.** Bluefen consent, the Riverlark release and the DD-005 bonuses are all unresolved. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter confirms each is outstanding.

The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026. That is about six weeks before today (5 November 2026), so each disclosed status needs to be brought down to date.

---

## Part A: Limitation of Liability

### 1. General cap (cl 12.1): 20% / AUD 4.8m
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% fallback needs prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft. None has been given.
- **Pushback:** Reject and restate 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not signal that 20% is available.

### 2. Thresholds (cl 12.2)
- **Seller's position:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery.
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery once the basket is exceeded.
- **Why it matters:** The de minimis is 5x ours and the basket is 5x ours. Combined with excess-only (deductible) recovery, we would absorb the first AUD 250k of loss outright. Aggregations of claims each under AUD 25k would never count at all.
- **Pushback:** Reject on all three elements and restate the playbook position.

### 3. Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller's position:** 18 months for general claims, plus a rule that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Playbook:** 24 months. The 18-month fallback needs Amelia Frost's approval, which has not been given.
- **The default rule is the more dangerous part.** It is a hidden general-regime override. It reverses the burden, so any category we fail to carve out expressly (Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, covenants, payment obligations) defaults into the general cap and time limit.
- **Pushback:** Restate 24 months. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default. Instead, list expressly which limitations apply to which category.

### 4. Fundamental / Title warranties
- **Seller's position:** same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Playbook:** a separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Why it matters:** Title to 100% of the shares is what we are paying AUD 24m for. Capping a title failure at AUD 4.8m with an 18-month window is commercially untenable. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason.
- **Pushback:** Reject outright. This is non-negotiable.

### 5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller's position:** these apply "to all Claims of any nature."
- **The gap:** the draft contains no fraud carve-out. Read literally, this would cap, time-bar and exclude claims for the Seller's own fraud or concealment. It would also bar reliance on pre-contract misrepresentations. It is likely partly unenforceable for fraud, but we should not rely on that.
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one has authority to waive this.
- **Pushback:** Insert a full carve-out covering the Seller, its officers, employees and advisers. Also confirm that specific indemnities, covenants and payment obligations sit outside the general regime.

---

## Part B: Disclosure and Buyer Knowledge

### 6. General disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller's position:** deemed disclosure of the whole data room (as at 22 September 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."
- **Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search disclosure.
- **Why it matters:** this would let the Seller rely on anything buried anywhere in the data room or public record to defeat a warranty claim.
- **Pushback:**
  - Delete 1.1 and 1.2.
  - Require each disclosure to be made against a specific warranty, in enough detail for us to assess its nature and scope.
  - Note that 1.4 (no admission) is acceptable in principle. It must not, however, dilute disclosures that are otherwise specific.
  - The letter jumps from 1.2 to 1.4. Ask for paragraph 1.3 or confirmation that it was intentionally deleted.

### 7. Buyer knowledge bar (cl 8.3)
- **Seller's position:** a blanket bar on claims for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, or that was "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Why it matters:** this is a second, back-door route to whole-data-room disclosure. It also covers constructive knowledge and all of our advisers.
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions.
- **Pushback:** Delete clause 8.3. If any knowledge qualifier survives, it must:
  - be framed as *Seller* knowledge, limited to named individuals after reasonable enquiry;
  - never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

---

## Part C: Completion Risks

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3; DD-002)
- **Facts disclosed:** about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30%. There is a change-control consent clause (11.2) with conditions (11.3). The Seller confirms it has **not** produced a final written consent or evidence that the conditions are satisfied.
- **Seller's position:** reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent.
- **Problems:**
  - Consent-on-delivery ignores the 11.3 conditions. A conditional consent could be "delivered" while the change-control right remains live.
  - Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a customer this material.
- **Pushback:** Make it a condition precedent that, before Completion, we receive:
  - an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) written consent from Bluefen; and
  - evidence satisfactory to us that each clause 11.3 condition has been met.

  Also add a Buyer right to waive or terminate, a stronger effort standard, and status reporting. Ask for a status update since 22 September.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7; DD-003)
- **Facts disclosed:** about AUD 3.2m outstanding, with a change-control provision (8.1) and a discharge provision (9.2). Not repaid; no discharge included.
- **Seller's position:** a release "to be provided following Completion."
- **Why it matters:** a change of control may trigger 8.1. We could then be paying full price for a company carrying a live AUD 3.2m facility and security, with only a post-Completion promise.
- **Playbook:** a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion.
- **Pushback:**
  - Require a payout letter dated close to Completion.
  - Require direct payment to Riverlark from the funds flow, treated as Debt within the debt-free price mechanics.
  - Require executed releases and discharges, including PPSR, delivered at Completion.
  - A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable Riverlark undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither currently exists.

### 10. DD-005 completion bonuses: AUD 420,000 plus on-costs
- **Facts disclosed:** conditional completion bonuses of AUD 420,000. They are omitted from the funds flow. The Disclosure Letter does not address payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs.
- **Seller's position:** a "matter for the Seller," not itemised.
- **Problem:** this is exactly the "silent exclusion" the playbook warns against. The bonuses are probably the Company's obligation. If they are not deducted or paid from the funds flow, the Company (now ours) bears AUD 420k plus on-costs after Completion. "A matter for the Seller" has no mechanism behind it.
- **Pushback:**
  - Require a specific funds flow line item, or treatment as Debt or a Transaction Expense deducted from price.
  - Cover the AUD 420,000 plus all triggered payroll tax, super, PAYG withholding and other on-costs.
  - Add a Seller indemnity for any shortfall or later-triggered amounts, outside the general cap and basket.
  - Request the bonus terms and the payroll tax and superannuation analysis.

---

## Part D: Specific Matters

### 11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DD-004, DD-010)
- **Facts disclosed:** under clause 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open. The Seller concedes this is not bank-verified, and there is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Seller's position:** the indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate."
- **Our view:** the AUD 180,000 is unverified in either direction, so we should not assume it is owed, paid, or the full exposure. The real risk is that the Company does not own IP it uses, which goes beyond the payment.
- **Pushback:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover any loss from any failure of IP ownership or transfer under DD-004. This includes third-party claims, re-development cost, and any additional fees or disputes.
  - Keep the SOW3 cure mechanism.
  - As a pre-Completion step, require payment evidence or a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay.
  - Keep the indemnity outside the general cap, basket and time limit.

### 12. Export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6; DD-006)
- **Facts disclosed:** a download link was sent to an unintended external address. The export may contain about 1,240 records. Access, scope and any notification duty are not established, and the investigation is preliminary.
- **Seller's position:** "not expected to be material."
- **Our view:** the Seller cannot know that yet, and we should not overstate it either. There is no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified loss.
- **Pushback:**
  - Reject any characterisation of the incident as immaterial.
  - Require preservation of logs and evidence.
  - Require a proper investigation, including an assessment under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme.
  - Require regular updates to us before Completion, and Buyer consultation on any notification decision.
  - Seek a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, outside the general limitations.
  - Ensure the general disclosure does not neutralise the privacy warranties.
  - Ask for the status since 22 September.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (DD-008, DD-011): AUD 330,000
- **Facts disclosed:** three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each. The Disclosure Letter itself says they should be read together for timing and scope. It does not say whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
- **Seller's position:** ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Our view:** that conclusion is not supported by the Seller's own letter. Equally, the playbook does not allow us to treat them automatically as Debt or a price deduction.
- **Pushback:** Reserve our position and assess. Ask for:
  - the contracts;
  - the timing relative to the sale process;
  - whether any amount was prepaid or accrued;
  - any termination rights and related-party links.

  Consider ordinary-course and no-new-commitment covenants for the period to Completion. Revisit the commercial treatment once the facts are in.

### 14. Title (DD-012)
- **Seller's position:** title is "evidenced by" the share register.
- **Our view:** the register is an internal record supplied by the Seller. It is not independent proof, and the Seller's letter (para 10) concedes we have not verified it.
- **Pushback:** Require independent evidence of:
  - ASIC records consistent with the register;
  - share issue and transfer history and share certificates;
  - absence of encumbrances (PPSR searches, and Riverlark security over the shares if any);
  - no options or convertibles outstanding;
  - Seller authority (board resolutions, constitution, any shareholder approvals).

  Title warranties must sit in the fundamental regime (see item 4).

### 15. Tax and IP warranties
- **Seller's position:** "settled under the general regime."
- **Our view:** they are not settled. Under the playbook both remain open, and we should not assume either unlimited liability or a resolution.
- **Pushback:** Record expressly that Tax and IP terms remain open. Do not let the "all Claims" default (item 3) settle them by omission. Keep them as separate categories.

### 16. Lower-priority confirmations
- **Office lease (DD-007):** the letter describes only a notification obligation. Confirm that no landlord consent is triggered, and add the notification to the Completion steps.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** the letter describes a restriction on assignment, not a change-of-control consent. Confirm that no change-of-control or deemed-assignment provision applies on a share sale.

Neither appears to be a consent condition on current information, but both should be confirmed rather than assumed.

---

## Summary of Recommendations

**Reject and restate our playbook position:**
1. Cap of 25% / AUD 6.0m (not 20%).
2. De minimis AUD 5k; basket AUD 50k; first-dollar recovery.
3. General claims period of 24 months (not 18). Delete the "limitations apply to all Claims" default.
4. A separate fundamental and title regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
5. A full fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out from all limitations, the exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
6. Specific fair disclosure only. Delete Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2, and query the missing 1.3.
7. Delete the cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge bar.

**Fix before Completion:**
8. Bluefen: effective consent plus evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a condition precedent.
9. Riverlark: current payout letter, direct repayment from the funds flow, and security releases at Completion.
10. DD-005 bonuses: AUD 420k plus on-costs as a funds flow line item or price deduction, backed by an indemnity.

**Specific protections:**
11. Ironquay: a broadened IP indemnity with the SOW3 cure preserved, plus payment or assignment evidence.
12. DD-006: preservation, investigation, updates and a specific indemnity, with no characterisation either way.
13. Sandbar: reserve our position pending information, with no automatic Debt treatment.
14. Title: independent verification beyond DD-012.
15. Tax and IP: record as open, in separate categories.
16. Lease and Mossvale: confirm the share sale triggers no consent.

**Process points:**
- **No fallback authority exists.** The negotiating team should not offer or accept the 20% cap or the 18-month period unless Amelia Frost gives written authority identifying this draft. If the team thinks either concession may become necessary, raise it with Amelia now rather than at the table.
- The fraud carve-out cannot be waived by anyone, including in negotiation.
- **Bring-down request:** the Disclosure Letter is dated 22 September 2026. Ask the Seller for an updated status on Bluefen, Riverlark, DD-006 and Ironquay, and require bring-down of the disclosures to signing and to Completion.

- **Why it matters:** a change of control may trigger 8.1. We could then be paying full price for a company carrying a live AUD 3.2m facility and security, with only a post-Completion promise.
- **Playbook:** a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion.
- **Pushback:**
  - Require a payout letter dated close to Completion.
  - Require direct payment to Riverlark from the funds flow, treated as Debt within the debt-free price mechanics.
  - Require executed releases and discharges, including PPSR, delivered at Completion.
  - A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable Riverlark undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither currently exists.

### 10. DD-005 completion bonuses: AUD 420,000 plus on-costs
- **Facts disclosed:** conditional completion bonuses of AUD 420,000. They are omitted from the funds flow. The Disclosure Letter does not address payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs.
- **Seller's position:** a "matter for the Seller," not itemised.
- **Problem:** this is exactly the "silent exclusion" the playbook warns against. The bonuses are probably the Company's obligation. If they are not deducted or paid from the funds flow, the Company (now ours) bears AUD 420k plus on-costs after Completion. "A matter for the Seller" has no mechanism behind it.
- **Pushback:**
  - Require a specific funds flow line item, or treatment as Debt or a Transaction Expense deducted from price.
  - Cover the AUD 420,000 plus all triggered payroll tax, super, PAYG withholding and other on-costs.
  - Add a Seller indemnity for any shortfall or later-triggered amounts, outside the general cap and basket.
  - Request the bonus terms and the payroll tax and superannuation analysis.

## Part D: Specific Matters

### 11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DD-004, DD-010)
- **Facts disclosed:** under clause 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open. The Seller concedes this is not bank-verified, and there is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Seller's position:** the indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate."
- **Our view:** the AUD 180,000 is unverified in either direction, so we should not assume it is owed, paid, or the full exposure. The real risk is that the Company does not own IP it uses, which goes beyond the payment.
- **Pushback:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover any loss from any failure of IP ownership or transfer under DD-004. This includes third-party claims, re-development cost, and any additional fees or disputes.
  - Keep the SOW3 cure mechanism.
  - As a pre-Completion step, require payment evidence or a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay.
  - Keep the indemnity outside the general cap, basket and time limit.

### 12. Export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6; DD-006)
- **Facts disclosed:** a download link was sent to an unintended external address. The export may contain about 1,240 records. Access, scope and any notification duty are not established, and the investigation is preliminary.
- **Seller's position:** "not expected to be material."
- **Our view:** the Seller cannot know that yet, and we should not overstate it either. There is no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified loss.
- **Pushback:**
  - Reject any characterisation of the incident as immaterial.
  - Require preservation of logs and evidence.
  - Require a proper investigation, including an assessment under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme.
  - Require regular updates to us before Completion, and Buyer consultation on any notification decision.
  - Seek a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, outside the general limitations.
  - Ensure the general disclosure does not neutralise the privacy warranties.
  - Ask for the status since 22 September.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (DD-008, DD-011): AUD 330,000
- **Facts disclosed:** three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each. The Disclosure Letter itself says they should be read together for timing and scope. It does not say whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
- **Seller's position:** ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Our view:** that conclusion is not supported by the Seller's own letter. Equally, the playbook does not allow us to treat them automatically as Debt or a price deduction.
- **Pushback:** Reserve our position and assess. Ask for:
  - the contracts;
  - the timing relative to the sale process;
  - whether any amount was prepaid or accrued;
  - any termination rights and related-party links.

  Consider ordinary-course and no-new-commitment covenants for the period to Completion. Revisit the commercial treatment once the facts are in.

### 14. Title (DD-012)
- **Seller's position:** title is "evidenced by" the share register.
- **Our view:** the register is an internal record supplied by the Seller. It is not independent proof, and the Seller's letter (para 10) concedes we have not verified it.
- **Pushback:** Require independent evidence of:
  - ASIC records consistent with the register;
  - share issue and transfer history and share certificates;
  - absence of encumbrances (PPSR searches, and Riverlark security over the shares if any);
  - no options or convertibles outstanding;
  - Seller authority (board resolutions, constitution, any shareholder approvals).

  Title warranties must sit in the fundamental regime (see item 4).

### 15. Tax and IP warranties
- **Seller's position:** "settled under the general regime."
- **Our view:** they are not settled. Under the playbook both remain open, and we should not assume either unlimited liability or a resolution.
- **Pushback:** Record expressly that Tax and IP terms remain open. Do not let the "all Claims" default (item 3) settle them by omission. Keep them as separate categories.

### 16. Lower-priority confirmations
- **Office lease (DD-007):** the letter describes only a notification obligation. Confirm that no landlord consent is triggered, and add the notification to the Completion steps.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** the letter describes a restriction on assignment, not a change-of-control consent. Confirm that no change-of-control or deemed-assignment provision applies on a share sale.

Neither appears to be a consent condition on current information, but both should be confirmed rather than assumed.

## Summary of Recommendations

**Reject and restate our playbook position:**
1. Cap of 25% / AUD 6.0m (not 20%).
2. De minimis AUD 5k; basket AUD 50k; first-dollar recovery.
3. General claims period of 24 months (not 18). Delete the "limitations apply to all Claims" default.
4. A separate fundamental and title regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
5. A full fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out from all limitations, the exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
6. Specific fair disclosure only. Delete Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2, and query the missing 1.3.
7. Delete the cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge bar.

**Fix before Completion:**
8. Bluefen: effective consent plus evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a condition precedent.
9. Riverlark: current payout letter, direct repayment from the funds flow, and security releases at Completion.
10. DD-005 bonuses: AUD 420k plus on-costs as a funds flow line item or price deduction, backed by an indemnity.

**Specific protections:**
11. Ironquay: a broadened IP indemnity with the SOW3 cure preserved, plus payment or assignment evidence.
12. DD-006: preservation, investigation, updates and a specific indemnity, with no characterisation either way.
13. Sandbar: reserve our position pending information, with no automatic Debt treatment.
14. Title: independent verification beyond DD-012.
15. Tax and IP: record as open, in separate categories.
16. Lease and Mossvale: confirm the share sale triggers no consent.

**Process points:**
- **No fallback authority exists.** The negotiating team should not offer or accept the 20% cap or the 18-month period unless Amelia Frost gives written authority identifying this draft. If the team thinks either concession may become necessary, raise it with Amelia now rather than at the table.
- The fraud carve-out cannot be waived by anyone, including in negotiation.
- **Bring-down request:** the Disclosure Letter is dated 22 September 2026. Ask the Seller for an updated status on Bluefen, Riverlark, DD-006 and Ironquay, and require bring-down of the disclosures to signing and to Completion.
